text:
maria: Heads up — after the control-plane upgrade to k8s 1.31 in eu-west-1 this morning, several GPU nodes are reporting allocatable nvidia.com/gpu: 0. Multiple pods stuck Pending.
jon: Ugh. Which image of the nvidia device plugin are we running? We had that 0-reporting bug months back on an old plugin.
alex: It's the DaemonSet v0.12.2 (from our infra helm chart). kubelet logs show device plugin registration OK, but node status shows capacity 0. Quick `kubectl get` below: 
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu
ip-10-0-5-123   Ready    5h   v1.31.0   192.168.5.12   <none>   0.10   0/24   0    nvidia.com/gpu:0
```
maria: And pods: 
```
$ kubectl describe pod gpu-inference-0 -n inference
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x3 over 4m)  default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 10 node(s) didn't have free GPUs
```
will: Did the nodes change labels or taints after the upgrade? autoscaler might be mis-evaluating available GPU capacity.
jon: Checked labels — instance-type label is still there but node-role/gpu label was stripped on two nodes during upgrade. Could be why scheduler thinks no GPU?
sre-oncall: infra-bot flagged several control-plane nodes with API churn between 1.30->1.31 for the cloud provider client. There was an upstream change to NodeStatus subresource serialization.
alex: Restarted device plugin pod on one affected node. After restart, plugin logs show it registered 8 GPUs, but the node's status remains showing 0. Seems like kubelet isn't updating node.status.capacity after device plugin registration.
maria: Temporary mitigation: cordon affected nodes and force drain + uncordon to trigger full re-registration? That risks evicting running GPU jobs. Any less disruptive option?
will: Can we patch the device-plugin to write to /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/restart-on-upgrade flag? Not ideal.
jon: Quick test: restarting kubelet on a single node fixed node.status for me in staging earlier (kubelet re-pushed node.Status). Suggest rolling kubelet restart via daemonset? But kubelet is static on our AMIs, not DS.
sre-oncall: I'm +1 for scheduled small restart window for kubelets on the affected pool, but we should coordinate with batch teams. Also file ticket to upstream — sounds like kubelet lost ability to reconcile device plugin capacity after the control-plane REST change.
infra-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-143, tagging oncall and owners. Link: https://redwood.internal/infra/incidents/INF-2026-143
maria: Ok, plan: (1) roll a safe kubelet restart on one node to validate (non-disruptive: drain with --ignore-daemonsets, evict best-effort only), (2) if fixed, schedule rolling kubelet restarts across pool with 10min stagger, (3) open hotfix PR to bump device-plugin to v0.13 which has reported upstream fixes for 1.31 compatibility.
alex: I'm running the staged restart on ip-10-0-5-123 now. Logs: 
```
systemctl restart kubelet
# tail -n 200 /var/log/messages | grep device-plugin
May 01 08:21:12 kubelet[1234]: device-plugin: registered 8 GPUs
May 01 08:21:14 kubelet[1234]: node/status update: nvidia.com/gpu=8
```
alex: After ~20s, kubectl shows capacity 8. GPU pods scheduled fine on that node.
maria: Nice. Can we automate detection to avoid manual restarts in future?
jon: We should add a readiness probe to node health check that verifies node.status allocatable for critical resource labels (nvidia.com/gpu) and alert if mismatch between device-plugin and node.status. Also an autoscaler patch to avoid scaling down nodes until node.status stabilizes for 30s.
will: Cost note: autoscaler already terminated 2 nodes earlier thinking they were underutilized (because node.Status=0). That caused a small blip; estimate ~0.7 GPU-hours wasted in eu-west-1. I'll add to the incident cost section.
sre-oncall: Recording mitigation steps in INF-2026-143 runbook. We should coordinate with AMI team to include kubelet args or a post-upgrade hook that forces kubelet to reconcile device-plugin endpoints.
maria: Adding owners: @alex (device-plugin), @jon (autoscaler), @will (cost), @sre-oncall (coord). Will push device-plugin bump PR and a small autoscaler guard today.
jon: I'll draft the autoscaler guard: check node.status allocatable for resource key before considering node removable; add 30s stabilization window.
maria: Thanks all. If anyone sees other pools with this pattern, ping here. :thumbsup:
